families.family: Ukraine macro-region first-stage contests (Eastern/Western/Southern/Northern/Central/Kyiv, briefly Southwestern)

facts.participants: These rows are Stage II ('регіональний етап', officially styled '1/4 першості світу') of the All-Ukrainian student programming olympiad/championship (AUCPC), run per macro-region at base universities; each region draws university teams (plus guest school teams) from several oblasts. ~40 teams onsite per region (LNU Western 2019: 40+ university teams; NUBiP Northern 2018: 41 teams from 20 institutions); the ~123 median in the archive is REGISTERED teams on the judge. Nationally Stage II hosts 200+ teams across ~5-6 base universities; top-200 of Stage I advance, max 8 teams/institution.
facts.problemset: SHARED-SIBLING SET, confirmed: 2025 regulations state Stage II 'проводиться одночасно в усіх базових навчальних закладах ІІ етапу із використанням спільного Інтернет-сервера' (simultaneously in all base institutions on a common Internet server); VNTU also states both stages use 'one and the same set of tasks' across sites. The regions are per-site rankings of one nationwide round, not independent problemsets. Judges over time: e-olymp (most years), ejudge at NUBiP 2018, Algotester since ~2023-2025 (icpc2025.algotester.com).
facts.qualification: Full chain verified: Stage I (oblast, '1/8 першості світу') -> Stage II (macro-region, '1/4') -> Stage III All-Ukrainian final -> SEERC (ICPC Southeastern Europe semifinal) -> World Finals. Stage II -> III quotas (2025 regs): one team per oblast if in national top-100 with nonzero score, plus ranking fill, max 3 teams/institution, 47 teams max at the Ukrainian venue; Stage III is run adjacent to SEERC's Ukrainian site (SEERC teams may sit at the Ukrainian Stage III venue by mutual consent; SEERC itself was hosted at VNTU Vinnytsia in 2018 and 2021, later Bucharest+Vinnytsia dual-site). Note the quotas are computed on the UNIFIED standings (per-oblast/per-institution), i.e. qualification depends on geography, not on which sibling region row you appear in.
facts.format: Onsite at regional base universities through 2019 (LNU Lviv, Sep 13-15 2019; NURE Kharkiv 2018; NUBiP Kyiv Sep 15 2018; ONAFT Odesa). 2020: online (NURE lists 'II етап ... 26.09.20, on-line') — COVID. 2021: ran (Stage II rank PDF exists), SEERC 2021 held online from Vinnytsia. 2022-2025: wartime — online; 2025 regulations codify it: 'Змагання ІІ етапу проводяться в онлайн-форматі', with teams optionally sitting offline at base institutions. 2022 Stage II ran with a reduced field (~46 scored teams).
facts.host: Base universities per region (as evidenced): Western = Ivan Franko LNU (Lviv); Eastern = NURE (Kharkiv; KhPI hosted the 2019 oblast stage); Northern = NUBiP (Kyiv; hosted the region ~5 times); Southern = ONAFT/ONTU (Odesa; also hosted the 2018 Stage III final); Central = VNTU (Vinnytsia, the national coordinating hub, olimp.vntu.edu.ua / olymp.vinnica.ua); Kyiv city ran as its own region in some years; a 'Southwestern' region existed at least in 2018 (ONTU document lists six regions incl. Southwestern, no Kyiv that year). Region set varied year to year.

for: R3: squarely on the WF path — Stage II gates Stage III and thence SEERC, with explicit published quotas (2025 regulations).
R1: each region spans many universities across several oblasts (41 teams / 20 institutions at NUBiP 2018) — not a local qualifier.
R4: onsite at base universities until 2019; online only from 2020 (COVID) and 2022+ (war) — fits the maintainer's force-majeure exception.

R2 (sibling-share clause): the simultaneous shared problemset across regions is exactly the documented-acceptable case — advancement quotas are geographic (per-oblast/per-institution), so qualification depends on the split.
against: Identity lens: regions have no jury, problemset, or identity of their own — they are venue-partitioned rankings of ONE nationwide round; the six per-region rows per year should be merged into a single contest with several site rankings (like multi-site SWERC), not six contests.
Region composition is unstable (Southwestern briefly, Kyiv sometimes separate, wartime consolidation), so per-region continuity is weak.
2020+ editions are online; mainline status of those years rests entirely on the COVID/war exception.
evidence: https://icpc2025.algotester.com/files/10100-icpc2025-regulations.pdf — official 2025 AUCPC regulations: 3 stages (1/8, 1/4 statuses), Stage II online + simultaneous on a common server, quotas Stage I->II (top-200, <=8/inst) and Stage II->III (per-oblast top-100, <=3/inst, 47 teams), SEERC co-location.
https://vntu.edu.ua/uk/acm/auspc.html — AUCPC structure: Stage II at five base universities, 200+ teams; Stage III with a group holding SEERC-semifinal rights.
https://olimp.vntu.edu.ua/uk/default/ — same task set across sites; SEERC hosted jointly Bucharest+Vinnytsia; SEERC 2021 online; 2019-2022 results.
https://lnu.edu.ua/u-l-vivs-komu-universyteti-startuvav-ii-etap-vseukrains-koi-students-koi-olimpiady-z-prohramuvannia/ — Western region Stage II onsite at LNU, Sep 13-15 2019, 40+ teams.
https://nubip.edu.ua/node/50140 — Northern region Stage II onsite at NUBiP Kyiv, Sep 15 2018, 41 teams/20 institutions, ejudge, 13 problems 5h.
https://software.nure.ua/olympiads/ — NURE (Kharkiv/Eastern): Stage II onsite 14-15.09.2018; Stage II 26.09.2020 'on-line' (COVID pivot); finals in Vinnytsia 2018-19.

https://www.kit.ontu.edu.ua/upload/file/olympics/student/2.pdf — 2018: six regions incl. Southwestern; Southern base = ONAFT Odesa; Stage III at ONAFT Oct 10-12 2018; SEERC (Vinnytsia, Oct 20-22 2018) as the semifinal track.
https://olimp.vntu.edu.ua/uk/aucpc-reg/2022-au2u/rezultaty/ — wartime 2022 Stage II ran, ~46 scored teams.

https://vntu.edu.ua/uk/news/student-kafedry-prohramnoho-zabezpechennya-stav-pryzerom-finalu-vseukrayinskoyi-studentskoyi-olimpiady-z-prohramuvannya-lnu-open-2026-5054.html — caution: 'LNU Open 2026' is the final of the INDIVIDUAL student olympiad (188 individuals, medals), a separate track from the team championship.

facts.participants: Open qualification stage of the ICPC Moscow subregional (четвертьфинал): any team of three students/postgrads from a Moscow-area university or college, unlimited teams per institution, free registration (327-423 teams in the archive years; 570+ teams from 20+ universities in 2025). Ineligible/school teams could enter unofficially.
facts.problemset: Its own problemset, distinct from the Moscow subregional's round (separate contest a few weeks earlier).
facts.qualification: Gates the Moscow subregional, which gates NERC (semifinal) and the WF. 2019: qualification Oct 6 at university venues -> quarterfinal Oct 26 (Music Media Dome). 2020: qualification 15.11 -> MRC main round; ~20 winning teams advanced from MRC to NERC. 2025 admission formula published: strongest team of each university (>=1 problem solved) + best floor(0.4X) teams + university quotas -> 122 invited teams at Skolkovo. Branding: 'Moscow Programming Contest' in 2018-2019 (organized with it-edu.com / Moscow education dept), then folded into the 'Moscow Regional Contest' as its 'отборочный этап' (organizers MSU + MIPT); by 2024-25 the whole MRC is marketed as '1/8 финала ICPC'.
facts.format: 2018-2019: onsite, distributed across many Moscow university venues simultaneously (HSE 2017 precedent; MSU news 2019; 13 sites in 2025). 2020: fully online on Yandex.Contest (COVID) — as was the quarterfinal. 2021-2022: online era continued (MRC 2021 site icpc.msu.ru; MRC 2022 hosted on official.contest.yandex.com/mrc2022). 2024-2025: back to in-person distributed (13 university sites).
facts.host: No single venue of its own: teams sit at their home universities' labs (multi-site). Organizers: MSU + MIPT (+ ЦПМ/it-edu in the MPC-branded years); Yandex sponsor/platform.

for: R3: it demonstrably gates the Moscow subregional (published selection formula; 2019/2020 news) — firmly on the WF path.
R1: dozens of institutions across the Moscow region — not a single-university qualifier.
R2: fresh problemset separate from the subregional.
against: Identity lens: same geography as its parent (Moscow subregional), no venue/community of its own — participants sit in their own universities; it is the subregional's qualification stage, structurally identical to the other NERC quals (family 3). The 2018-19 'Moscow Programming Contest' brand is the only own-identity element, and it was later absorbed into 'Moscow Regional Contest — отборочный этап'.
R4: 2020-2022 editions were online (2020-21 excusable as COVID; 2022 online by inertia/design — no exception applies).
evidence: https://cs.msu.ru/news/3048 — 2019: 'квалификационный, отборочный этап' Oct 6 at Moscow universities -> quarterfinal Oct 26 at Music Media Dome; free, teams of 3; icpc@it-edu.com contact.
https://www.hse.ru/news/edu/210162763.html — 2017: the qualification held at multiple Moscow venues (HSE site among them); ICPC eligibility rules; open to HSE and other universities.

https://cs.msu.ru/news/3408 — MRC 2020: qualification 15.11.2020, entirely online on Yandex.Contest; open to any Moscow-area university/college, unlimited teams; MRC = quarterfinal; ~20 teams advance to NERC.
https://moscow.nerc.icpc.global/ — 2025: qualification in person across 13 university sites, 570+ teams; explicit admission formula to the main contest (122 teams, Skolkovo); organizers MSU/MIPT.
https://official.contest.yandex.com/mrc2022/?lang=en — MRC 2022 ran on Yandex.Contest (trial + main), i.e. online era still in 2022.
https://it-edu.com/pages/icpc/ — organizer page titled 'Moscow Programming Contest 2019' (JS-only, content not fetchable; brand evidence).
https://phystech-union.org/otkryta-registraciya-komand-na-moscow-regional-contest-1-8-finala-icpc-2024-2025/ — MRC marketed as '1/8 финала ICPC 2024-2025' (search result title; stage-tier branding).

facts.participants: Each NERC subregional (Northwestern/Northern at ITMO, Moscow, Southern & Volga at SGU Saratov, Ural, Belarus/Western, Kazakhstan, Central Russia, Siberia, Caucasus/Central-Asia regions...) runs its own qualification round ('отборочный', tier-branded '1/8 финала ICPC') a few weeks before the subregional; open mass entry (median ~174 teams; Moscow 570+, Kazakhstan 185).
facts.problemset: NO evidence of a shared problemset across different subregions' quals: each is prepared and dated independently by its subregional's organizers (2025 qual dates spread from Sep 27 to Nov 2 across regions; NWRRC quals have their own Codeforces gym mirrors; Southern qual a separate Codeforces round; Belarus qual is the BSU Championship on iRunner). Unlike the Ukrainian macro-regions, these are genuinely distinct contests per subregion.
facts.qualification: They gate admission to their subregional (quarterfinal), which gates NERC: Moscow publishes an explicit formula (strongest team per university + best 40% + quotas); EKTU/CPFed: 'На каждом этапе соревнования проводится отбор для прохождения на следующий'; BSU: advancing teams progress to the Belarus championship in Minsk and then the semifinal in St. Petersburg.
facts.format: Predominantly ONLINE BY DESIGN (not COVID-driven): NWRRC qualification 2019-2025 online with Codeforces mirrors (gym/102375, 104014, 105424); Southern 2024 qual on Codeforces; Moscow qual online 2020-2023 (Yandex.Contest). Exceptions run onsite/distributed-onsite: Moscow qual 2018-19 and 2024-25 (13 university sites), Kazakhstan Octafinal ('в очном формате, в стенах ВУЗа'), Belarus BSU Championship (onsite at BSU, hybrid/online 2023).
facts.host: Run by the subregional organizers (ITMO for NWRRC, MSU/MIPT for Moscow, SGU for Southern/Volga, BSU for Belarus, CPFed for Kazakhstan); teams sit online or at their home universities — the rounds have no venue of their own.

for: R3: they gate entry/allocation into the subregionals, hence are on the WF path.
R2: each subregion's qual uses its own fresh problemset (no cross-subregion sharing found).
against: R4: online by design for most subregions and years — the COVID exception does not cover them (NWRRC qual was online already in 2019 and still is in 2025).

Identity lens: anonymous 'Qualification' rounds with the same geography as their parent subregional and no name/venue/community of their own -> part of the parent. The exceptions that DO have identity are better handled individually: Moscow Programming Contest (family 2), BSU Championship/'Чемпионат БГУ' (an open championship doubling as Belarus qualification), Kazakhstan Octafinal (family 5).
evidence: https://neerc.ifmo.ru/subregions/northern.html — NWRRC archive: 'Qualification' sections 2019, 2021-2025, online rounds with Codeforces gym mirrors; main contest onsite at ITMO (Nov 15, 2025 quarterfinal).

https://nerc.itmo.ru/subregions/index.html — all NERC regional contests with TWO dates each (qual + main), dates differing per region (Southern Oct 5, Moscow Oct 12, Ural Oct 18, NWRRC/Azerbaijan/Kazakhstan Oct 26, ...) — independent rounds, not one shared set.
https://nerc.itmo.ru/subregions/southern.html — Southern & Volga (SGU Saratov): 2024 qualification standings on Codeforces (online).
https://moscow.nerc.icpc.global/ — Moscow qual gating formula and 2025 in-person 13-site format.

https://acm.bsu.by/events/bsu2023/ — 'Чемпионат БГУ 2023 (1/8 финала ICPC 2023-2024, квалификация Беларуси)': Belarusian universities, iRunner platform, 2023 hybrid (teams at their own universities), advancing to Minsk championship then the St. Petersburg semifinal.
https://www.ektu.kz/lastevents/federaciya_sportivnogo_programmirovaniya_zapuskaet_registraciyu_na_18_finala_icpc.aspx — CPFed: selection at each stage; the 1/8 tier feeding the quarterfinal.
https://codeforces.com/gym/105424 (and gym/104014, gym/102375) — NWRRC qualification mirrors on Codeforces (referenced from the NWRRC archive page; codeforces.com itself 403s the fetcher).

facts.participants: Student teams of the three Slovenian universities; rounds sat simultaneously at UL FRI (Ljubljana), UM FERI (Maribor) and UP FAMNIT (Koper).
facts.problemset: One set per round on the shared Putka judge (putka-upm.acm.si) for all three sites; rounds are numbered legs of one season, not named events.
facts.qualification: Individual rounds gate nothing by themselves: season scoring is cumulative ('best two rounds' count, finale problems worth double), and it is the season/finale result that selects Slovenian teams for ICPC CERC (e.g. 2007: 'štiri najboljše ekipe potujejo na srednjeevropsko tekmovanje v Prago').
facts.format: Season = trial round + 3 preliminary rounds + finale; rounds in-person in computer labs at the three faculties simultaneously (with online options in some years); running since ~1998 (10th finale in 2007).
facts.host: Jointly organized by UL FRI, UM FERI, UP FAMNIT under ACM Slovenia.

for: The season-level UPM satisfies R3 historically (CERC selection) — but that credit belongs to the already-catalogued year-long UPM, not to the individual rounds.
against: Identity lens: a numbered 'krog' has no own name, venue-identity or community — it is a leg of the marathon; cumulative best-2-of-3 + double-point finale scoring makes single rounds meaningless in isolation (R3 fails at round granularity).
R1 borderline at round level too: three universities' sites of one national event.
evidence: https://tekmovanja.acm.si/?q=upm — ACM Slovenia: trial + three preliminary rounds + finale; simultaneous at UL FRI / UM FERI / UP FAMNIT; Putka judge; best-two-rounds cumulative scoring, finale double points; best teams represent their universities at CERC.
https://www.monitor.si/novica/10-univerzitetni-programerski-maraton-koncan/135969/ — 2007 = 10th finale (UPM since ~1998); top 4 teams to CERC Prague.
https://putka-upm.acm.si/ — the Putka judge instance for UPM (round archive).

facts.participants: 185 teams (archive) from universities across Kazakhstan; teams compete at their own universities nationwide.
facts.problemset: Own round prepared under CPFed (Federation of Sport Programming of Kazakhstan); no evidence of reuse or sharing with another round (not independently verified).
facts.qualification: The '1/8 финала ICPC' tier of Kazakhstan's chain: Octafinal -> Kazakhstan Regional Contest (quarterfinal; 2023 onsite at Kostanay Regional University; 2025 Almaty + Astana) -> NERC (semifinal) -> WF. CPFed: 'На каждом этапе соревнования проводится отбор для прохождения на следующий'. It is an ICPC-registered contest with its own icpc.global finder entry and standings (kaz-icpc-qual-two).
facts.format: ONSITE, distributed: 'в очном формате, в стенах ВУЗа' (in person, on university premises); 2024-25 season: practice/qualification Oct 27, main contest Nov 3.
facts.host: CPFed Kazakhstan (cpfed.kz) as organizer; participating universities as sites (e.g. EKTU Oskemen announcement); registration via icpc.global.

for: R3: gates the Kazakhstan quarterfinal -> NERC -> WF; runs BEFORE what it feeds (Oct 27/Nov 3 ahead of the Nov 15 regional).
R4: onsite (distributed multi-site, but in-person) — unlike most NERC quals.
R1: nationwide, many universities.
Own identity markers: its own ICPC finder listing, standings, and CPFed branding ('Octafinal').
against: Identity lens counterargument: same geography as its parent (Kazakhstan Regional), teams sit at home universities, and the name is a tier label ('1/8 финала') — the same reasoning that files the other NERC quals under their parents; consistency would argue part-of-parent.
Only one/two editions so far (from 2024); problem originality not independently verified (R2 unproven).
Distributed-onsite is weaker than a single-venue onsite under R4's spirit.
evidence: https://www.ektu.kz/lastevents/federaciya_sportivnogo_programmirovaniya_zapuskaet_registraciyu_na_18_finala_icpc.aspx — CPFed registration for the 1/8 final: onsite at universities, Oct 27 + Nov 3, selection to the quarterfinal, registration via the icpc.global finder entry.
https://icpc.global/regionals/finder/kaz-icpc-qual-two — 'The 2024 ICPC Kazakhstan Octafinal' official ICPC listing (SPA; standings at .../kaz-icpc-qual-two-2025/standings).

https://ksu.edu.kz/ru/announcements/chetvertfinal-mezhdunarodnogo-chempionata-po-programmirovaniyu-icpc-kazakhstan-regional-contest/ — the parent tier: Kazakhstan Regional Contest = quarterfinal, onsite (Kostanay 2023), organized with cpfed.kz.
https://nerc.itmo.ru/subregions/index.html — Kazakhstan regional (Almaty; Astana) dated Nov 15 2025 with an Oct 26 earlier round — the octafinal/qualification slot in the NERC calendar.

facts.participants: National inter-university contest: ~16-19 teams from ~7+ Portuguese higher-education institutions per year (2016: 16 teams / 7 schools; 2021: 19 teams), max 2 teams per school, teams of 3, 5 hours, ICPC rules.
facts.problemset: Own fresh set each year (e.g. 9 problems in 2016) by a scientific committee drawn from several universities (Coimbra, Porto, Aveiro, Algarve, Lisbon in 2022) — no reuse found.
facts.qualification: NOT a formal gate to anything ICPC: SWERC is open to universities of Portugal/Spain/France/Italy/Switzerland/Israel etc. with direct per-university registration, and no SWERC or MIUP page documents MIUP-based slots. News language is 'preparacao dos alunos portugueses para a prova regional do Sudoeste Europeu (SWERC)' and, loosely, 'as melhores equipas da MIUP'2021 vao agora representar Portugal no SWERC' — de facto overlap/selection culture, not a qualification rule. MIUP runs Sep/Oct, before SWERC (Nov) — so timing would allow feeding, but no gate exists.
facts.format: Onsite, single venue, rotating host university each year: 2012 FCUP Porto, 2016 FCT NOVA, 2017 U. Minho, 2019 & 2021 IST Lisbon, 2022 U. Coimbra (Oct 15, in person), 2025 U. Aveiro. ~20th edition in 2021, i.e. running since ~2001.
facts.host: Rotates among Portuguese universities; organized by the host's informatics department with a multi-university scientific committee.

for: R1: genuinely multi-university and national (not a local qualifier).
R2: unique new problems each year by a national committee.
R4: onsite throughout, single venue.
against: R3: placement gates nothing — SWERC entry is by open university registration; MIUP is best read as the independent national championship (the KTH-contest case). The 'best teams go on to SWERC' news phrasing reflects overlap, not a rule.
evidence: https://dei.uc.pt/miup/ — MIUP 2022: Oct 15 2022, in person at U. Coimbra; max 2 teams/school; teams of 3, 5h; multi-university scientific committee.

https://sigarra.up.pt/fcup/en/noticias_geral.ver_noticia?p_nr=78113 — MIUP'2021 = 20th edition, 19 teams, IST host; 'melhores equipas ... vao agora representar Portugal no SWERC' (SWERC as the ICPC semifinal-tier phase).
https://www.di.fct.unl.pt/en/node/1542 — MIUP 2016 at FCT NOVA: 16 teams / 7 schools; described 'como preparacao ... para a prova regional do Sudoeste Europeu (SWERC)'.
https://swerc.eu/2024/ — SWERC 2024-25: open to teams from PT/ES/FR/IT/CH/IL (+microstates), three simultaneous sites (Porto, Lyon, Pisa); no national-contest qualification mentioned.
https://miup.web.ua.pt/ — MIUP 2025 hosted at U. Aveiro (JS-only site; host rotation evidence).

facts.participants: 'AdaByron: Concurso Universitario de Programacion' — NOT the Ada Byron Award (the U. Deusto prize for women technologists is unrelated). Two-tier national family: regional contests (2024: Andalucia, Castilla-La Mancha, Galicia, Madrid, Murcia, Valencia + a 'regional multisede' pooling 11+ other universities — 67 teams at the 2026 multisede) feeding a Concurso Nacional (the archive's 37-47-team rows). Madrid regional alone covers the six public Madrid universities. Teams of 3 students, 8-12 problems, 5 hours.
facts.problemset: Own sets per phase (regional and national are separate rounds run by the organizing universities; multisede sites share one set within a regional — internal sibling-share at the regional tier).
facts.qualification: Regionals gate the national final (internal chain). The FAMILY as a whole gates nothing ICPC: its stated objective is merely 'incentivar la participacion de los estudiantes ... en el concurso internacional de programacion ICPC'; no SWERC mention anywhere on ada-byron.es or SWERC's site. Timing reinforces this: the 2024 national ran July 5-6, AFTER the SWERC (Nov 2023) it would logically feed — the R3 trap the maintainer flagged.
facts.format: Onsite: regionals at each site (multisede = simultaneous university sites), national final in person (2024: July 5-6, Facultad de Informatica, Universidad Complutense de Madrid). XII edicion in 2026 => running since ~2014/15.
facts.host: Organized by a consortium of Spanish (public) universities; national host varies (UCM Madrid in 2024); sponsors IMDEA, Next Digital, Denodo, Bending Spoons.

for: R1: multi-university at every tier (six Madrid universities in one regional; 11+ universities in the multisede; national final nationwide).
R2: own problems; the multisede shared set is within one regional, reportable but internal.
R4: onsite.
against: R3: independent of the ICPC chain — encouragement of ICPC participation is a stated goal, not a qualification link; the July date puts it after SWERC in the season. Registry, same drawer as MIUP/KTH-style national championships.
evidence: https://ada-byron.es/2024/nac/programa.php — Concurso Nacional 2024: July 5-6 2024 at Facultad de Informatica UCM (onsite); six regional feeders + multisede; sponsors; no ICPC/SWERC mention.

https://ada-byron.es/2026/reg/multisede/clasificacion.php — XII edicion multisede regional: 67 teams from 11+ universities (UPC, UIB, USAL, Oviedo, La Rioja, UVA, Navarra x2, UEX, EHU, URV, ULL), Mar 25 2026; Regionales -> Nacional navigation.

https://blogs.upm.es/actividadesacreditables/ada-byron-concurso-de-programacion-c11045/ — Madrid regional: six public Madrid universities, in-person, teams of 3, 8-12 problems/5h; objective 'incentivar la participacion ... en el ... ICPC' (no qualification link).
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ada_Byron_Award — the unrelated Ada Byron prize (disambiguation guard).
https://ada-byron.es/2024/nac/ — national-final section (root redirect-loops for fetchers; inner .php pages load).

facts.participants: No evidence found that a Moldovan national/inter-university ICPC selection contest actually runs. Searches across the Education Ministry (mec.gov.md/mecc.gov.md), UTM/FCIM pages, and Moldovan press surface only SCHOOL-level republican olympiads — 'Olimpiada Republicana la Informatica' for grades 9-12 (154 pupils in 2023, held at UTM/Tekwill, organized by ANCE under the Ministry) — plus unrelated university contests (e.g. FCIM's PLC contest 'CIRCLE'). Nothing university-level and ICPC-shaped.
facts.problemset: Unknown — no published results, scoreboards or problem archives of any Moldovan university selection were found anywhere (11 shells x 11 seasons 2014-2024 matches one-per-year provisioning that never got used or never got published).
facts.qualification: Moldova is inside SEERC's catchment; SEERC entry is by direct per-university registration (no national gate required), so Moldovan universities (UTM, USM, ASEM appear in older SEERC team lists, e.g. 2016) can and do register directly. SEERC 2023's published top standings show Ukrainian/Romanian/Serbian teams, no Moldovan team sighted — consistent with sparse direct participation rather than a national pipeline.
facts.format: N/A — nothing verifiably ran. The school republican olympiad is onsite (Chisinau).
facts.host: The empty shells are most plausibly CMS instances provisioned annually (CMS is the judge used for Moldovan olympiad infrastructure) for a planned national round or the school olympiad's university-hosted infrastructure; no organizer statement found.

for: Nothing qualifies: no participants, no results, no problemsets, no gating role demonstrable for any year.
against: R2/R3 unверifiable: an event with no evidence of having been held cannot be a real contest in the archive (and if something did run privately, its results gate nothing visible — SEERC needs no national stage).
R1 risk if anything did run: with only a handful of Chisinau universities (UTM/USM/ASEM), any selection would look like a local qualifier.
evidence: https://mec.gov.md/ro/content/la-chisinau-inceput-olimpiada-republicana-la-informatica — the republican informatics olympiad is for school pupils (grades 9-12), at UTM/Tekwill, ANCE-organized; no university tier mentioned.
https://mecc.gov.md/en/node/17032 — ministry olympiad pages cover junior/school science olympiads only.

https://fcim.utm.md/noutate/circle-concursul-de-programare-a-automatelor-logice-programabile-plc/ — FCIM UTM's promoted contests are unrelated (PLC programming); no ICPC selection on the faculty site.

https://swerc.eu/2024/ + https://icpc.global/regionals/finder/seerc-2017/teams — ICPC regional entry is direct per-university registration; SEERC 2016 team lists include Moldovan universities (finder is an SPA, limited verification).
https://codeforces.com/blog/entry/123138 — SEERC 2023 (Universal Cup stage): published top standings show UA/RO/RS teams; no Moldovan university visible.

notes: NERC tier vocabulary decoder (useful across families 2, 3, 5): the per-subregion qualification rounds are branded '1/8 финала ICPC' (octafinal tier), the subregionals 'четвертьфинал' (quarterfinal), NERC itself is the semifinal. Kazakhstan's 'Octafinal' and Belarus's 'Чемпионат БГУ (1/8 финала, квалификация Беларуси)' and Moscow's qualification are all instances of the same tier — recommend one consistent archive policy for the tier (part-of-parent by default; promote only those with real own identity AND onsite format, per R4).

Ukraine sibling-set report (R2 clause): the macro-region rows are per-site rankings of ONE simultaneous nationwide round on a shared server; advancement quotas (per-oblast, per-institution, national top-100) are computed on unified results, so qualification depends on geography rather than on the region split — merge each year's regions into one contest with several rankings rather than dropping them as problem-reusers.

Ukraine judges/hosting drifted: e-olymp (Zhytomyr) most years, ejudge at NUBiP 2018, Algotester (Lviv) runs icpc2025.algotester.com; SEERC has been (co-)hosted at VNTU Vinnytsia since 2018 (2021 online edition run from Vinnytsia; later Bucharest+Vinnytsia dual site), and the 2025 regulations let SEERC teams sit at the Ukrainian Stage III venue (<=47 Ukrainian teams).

Beware conflation in Ukraine post-2024: 'LNU Open 2026' (Lviv) is the final of the INDIVIDUAL All-Ukrainian student programming olympiad (188 individuals, medal-based), a separate track from the team AUCPC/ICPC chain.
